value.name: confirms others knew
value.description: Marcus confirms that the others in the room already understood the house was being kept.
evidence: "I suspected. The brother who refuses to read his own ultimatum is not a brother who is going to sell. The sister who hid the letter is not a sister who is going to let him. The housekeeper who waited thirty-one years to speak was not waiting in order to watch the house go to strangers. The only person in the room on Thursday who did not know they were keeping the house was you, and that was because you were the only person in the room whose job required not knowing it until they told you."

value.name: accepts the explanation
value.description: The listener acknowledges Marcus's explanation and accepts that the situation was not obvious to them.

value.name: Marcus reassures listener
value.description: Marcus tells the listener not to be embarrassed and frames his own role as one of assumption and inference.
evidence: "Do not be embarrassed. It is your job not to assume. It is my job to assume. That is why there are two of us."

value.name: confirms Tuesday lunch
value.description: Marcus and the listener reaffirm that their Tuesday lunch plans remain in place.

value.name: reviews probate strategies
value.description: After the call, she studies the agenda and considers legal and financial ways to keep the house out of a forced sale.
evidence: She hung up and looked at the agenda and thought about what structures were available to a brother and a sister and a non-relative who wished to retain a house in probate against the pressure of debts that would not retreat just because the house was being kept.

value.name: considers sibling buyout
value.description: She identifies a buyout of one sibling's interest by the other as one possible solution.
evidence: There were several. There was a buyout of one sibling's interest by the other, financed by a mortgage.

value.name: considers partition agreement
value.description: She considers a partition agreement that would let the family share use of the house without forcing a sale.
evidence: There was a partition agreement that allocated use without forcing sale.

value.name: considers life estate for Rosa
value.description: She considers formalizing Rosa's right to remain in the house through a life estate.
evidence: There was a life estate carved out for Rosa, formalizing what the codicil had already informally accomplished.

value.name: considers renting third-floor apartment
value.description: She considers renting the separate third-floor apartment to generate income and help cover the debts.
